summary: A 30 μg optical micromirror, made of a silicon membrane with a high-reflectivity dielectric stack attached to superconducting microspheres, is stably levitated in a magnetic quadrupole field at cryogenic temperature. With magnetic feedback stabilizing the transverse motion, optical interferometry of the axial displacement reaches a sensitivity of order 100 pm/$\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ near the 167 Hz axial trap frequency.
motivation: Free-standing mirrors with minimal dissipation and tunable oscillation frequency would open precision sensing and quantum cavity optomechanics in the microgram mass regime.
method: Superconducting magnetic levitation of the mirror assembly in a quadrupole trap, magnetic feedback on the transverse modes, and interferometric readout of the axial mode.
result: Stable levitation of a 30 μg high-reflectivity mirror with displacement sensitivity of order 100 pm/$\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ near the 167 Hz axial trap frequency.
